+# Freebuff Tool Mapping
+
+Skills speak in actions ("dispatch a subagent", "create a todo", "read a file"). On Freebuff these resolve to the tools below.
+
+| Action skills request | Freebuff equivalent |
+| --- | --- |
+| Invoke or load a skill | `skill` with the skill directory name (for example `{"name": "brainstorming"}`) |
+| Create a todo / mark one complete | `write_todos` (rewrite the whole list each call) |
+| Read a file | `read_files` |
+| Create or overwrite a file | `write_file` |
+| Edit a file in place | `str_replace` |
+| Delete, move, or rename a file | `run_terminal_command` (`rm`, `mv`) |
+| Run a shell command | `run_terminal_command` |
+| Search file contents | `code_search` (ripgrep regex; pass `-F` in `flags` for literal text) |
+| Find files by name | `glob` |
+| List a directory | `list_directory` |
+| Fetch a URL | `read_url` |
+| Search the web | `web_search` |
+| Ask your human partner a question | `ask_user` |
+| Dispatch a subagent (`Subagent (general-purpose):` template) | No subagent tool is exposed. Do not fabricate a dispatch; use `executing-plans` and do the work inline. For a second pair of eyes, use the `requesting-code-review` reviewer prompt as a structured self-review, or ask your human partner to start a fresh session. |
+| Enter plan mode | Freebuff has no plan mode. Write designs to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and plans to `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md` with `write_file`. |
+| Persist progress across compaction | Write the ledger and briefs under `.superpowers/sdd/<plan-basename>/` (see `executing-plans`); `write_todos` is a live view, not durable storage. |
+
+## Skill discovery
+
+Freebuff discovers project skills in `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` and lists each skill's name and description in the system prompt. Load a skill by name with the `skill` tool. Reading a `SKILL.md` with `read_files` is only a fallback if the `skill` tool fails; prefer the tool.
+
+## Subagents
+
+This CLI exposes no subagent or task-dispatch tool. Skills that mention `Subagent (general-purpose):` must use their inline fallback:
+
+- `subagent-driven-development` → use `executing-plans` instead.
+- `dispatching-parallel-agents` → do the independent tasks sequentially, or explain that parallel dispatch is unavailable.
+
+Never invent `Task`, `subagent`, or similar tool calls.
+
+## Todos and durable state
+
+`write_todos` is the live progress view; update it after each completed item. Freebuff can compact context, so also keep the durable ledger from `executing-plans` in `.superpowers/sdd/<plan-basename>/progress.md`.

+**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action** — including clarifying questions, exploring the codebase, or checking files. If it turns out wrong for the situation, you don't have to use it.

+
+When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.

+| "I remember this skill" | Skills evolve. Read current version. |
+| "This doesn't count as a task" | Action = task. Check for skills. |
+| "The skill is overkill" | Simple things become complex. Use it. |
+| "I'll just do this one thing first" | Check BEFORE doing anything. |
+| "This feels productive" | Undisciplined action wastes time. Skills prevent it. |
+| "I know what that means" | Knowing the concept ≠ using the skill. Invoke it. |

# Agentic ODI [![CI](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/) [![uv](https://img.shields.io/badge/uv-managed-green)](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) [![Ruff](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/ruff/main/assets/badge/v2.json)](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff) [![FastMCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastMCP-powered-orange)](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) [![pytest](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-pytest-blue)](https://pytest.org) [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/Model%20Context%20Protocol-enabled-8A2BE2)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) > **Experimental test to learn and evaluate the feasibility of utilizing Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) specifications.**
--- ## 📋 Table of Contents - [The Vision: Context-Aware Innovation](#-the-vision-context-aware-innovation) - [Current State (Experimental Testbed)](#-current-state-experimental-testbed) - [Code Overview](#-code-overview) - [Getting Started](#-getting-started) - [Command-Line Interface (CLI)](#-command-line-interface-cli) - [Manage Customer Outcomes](#-manage-customer-outcomes) - [External Connectors (MCP Ingest)](#-external-connectors-mcp-ingest) - [One-Command Launch](#-one-command-launch-recommended) - [Manual Split-Terminal](#-manual-split-terminal-alternative) - [Local Tools-Capable LLM Backend](#-local-tools-capable-llm-backend-for-mcp-testing) - [Agent-Driven Testing](#-agent-driven-testing) - [Linting, Formatting & Type Checks](#-linting-formatting--type-checks-ci-parity) - [Testing](#-testing) - [Test Coverage Map](#-test-coverage-map) - [Agent Session Tracking](#-agent-session-tracking) - [Superpowers with Pi](#-superpowers-with-pi) - [Developer Workflow for Formatting](#-developer-workflow-for-formatting) +- [Superpowers with Freebuff](#-superpowers-with-freebuff) - [Deployment](#-deployment) - [Roadmap & Next Steps](#-roadmap--next-steps) - [Contributing](#-contributing) - [License](#-license) --- ## 🌟 The Vision: Context-Aware Innovation **Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)**, built on the "Jobs-to-be-Done" theory, relies on deeply understanding customer needs, desired outcomes, and execution contexts. Historically, applying ODI requires meticulous research, structured data modeling, and rigorous analysis. **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** represents a paradigm shift in how AI systems consume and reason over external context. By adopting MCP, we can bridge the gap between static user research and dynamic, agentic AI. The vision for **Agentic ODI** is to build a unified, open protocol where LLMs and autonomous agents can natively query, understand, and reason over ODI data (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores) dynamically in real-time. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server will act as the "brain" of customer needs, allowing agents to invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions strictly anchored in verified user outcomes. --- ## 🏗️ Current State (Experimental Testbed) This repository serves as an initial sandbox for understanding server-client MCP communication streams. We are utilizing [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) to prototype HTTP-based context delivery. --- ## 🧩 Code Overview This repository is a [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) made up of **six** installable projects, each with its own `pyproject.toml`, `src/` layout, and tests: | Package | Description | |---|---| | **`core/`** (`agentic-odi-core`) | Domain models, the `ODIService` business-logic layer, and repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite), including ODI opportunity-score computation. | | **`mcp_server/`** (`agentic-odi-mcp-server`) | A foundational MCP Server exposing an HTTP transport layer. It hosts tools for Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, and Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value). | | **`local_server/`** (`agentic-odi-local-server`) | A local FastAPI server that talks to the repository directly (no MCP transport). | | **`client/`** (`agentic-odi-client`) | **The Living Studio** — a spatial, conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation. Provides an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous conversational agent connected to the MCP server. It also hosts `run.py`, the local dev launcher that starts the server and the Studio UI together. | | **`cli/`** (`agentic-odi-cli`) | A [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based command-line interface. It provides version/help plus `outcomes` and `connectors` commands. | | **`connectors/`** (`agentic-odi-connectors`) | Pluggable external integrations. The first kind is an **MCP client connector** that connects to a remote MCP server over HTTP, checks health, and ingests tools/resources into a local ingest sink. Additional kinds (REST, webhooks, and so on) can register against the same protocol later. | --- ## 🚀 Getting Started ### Prerequisites - **Python** 3.10+ - [**uv**](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager Install the entire workspace (all six projects plus dev tooling): ```bash uv sync --all-packages ``` This creates a `.venv` and installs `agentic-odi-core`, `agentic-odi-mcp-server`, `agentic-odi-local-server`, `agentic-odi-client`, `agentic-odi-cli`, and `agentic-odi-connectors` in editable mode. ### 💻 Command-Line Interface (CLI) The [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based CLI lets you interact with Agentic ODI directly from your terminal — no chat UI required. It provides version and help information plus commands for connecting to external systems. Over time it will also expose commands for working with the ODI dataset (Jobs, Steps, and Outcomes). Launch it with: ```bash python -m cli --version # print the Agentic ODI version python -m cli --help # show available options and commands python -m cli # show help when no command is given ``` A console script is also installed, so `agentic-odi --version` works the same way. ### 🎯 Manage Customer Outcomes Manage Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value) via the CLI. The CLI acts as an MCP client, so the server must be running (`python -m mcp_server`): ```bash # Add a Customer Outcome agentic-odi outcomes add --job-id --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 --category cost_reduction --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn" # List outcomes (optionally filtered) agentic-odi outcomes list agentic-odi outcomes list --job-id # Get, update, delete agentic-odi outcomes get agentic-odi outcomes update --importance 9.0 agentic-odi outcomes delete --yes # Compute ODI Opportunity Score agentic-odi outcomes score 8 2 ``` Set `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` to point to a non-default server if needed. ### 🔌 External Connectors (MCP Ingest) Connectors are named integrations stored in `.agentic-odi/connectors.json` (or a path you pass with `--config` / `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_FILE`). The first kind is `mcp`: Agentic ODI acts as an MCP **client** and pulls catalog, resources, and optional tool results from an external MCP **server**. ```bash python -m cli connectors add mcp --name gong --url http://localhost:9000/mcp --tool latest_quote python -m cli connectors list python -m cli connectors health --name gong python -m cli connectors ingest --name gong ``` Ingested records are normalized (`catalog`, `resource`, `tool_result`) and appended to the in-process ingest sink. They are not written into the ODI jobs/outcomes store. ### ⚡ One-Command Launch (recommended) `python -m client.run` starts both the MCP server and the Studio UI concurrently. Press **Ctrl+C** to stop both. ```bash python -m client.run ``` | Service | URL | |---|---| | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp | | The Living Studio UI | http://localhost:8501 | ### 🔧 Manual Split-Terminal (alternative) Open two terminals and run each process separately: ```bash # Terminal 1 — MCP server python -m mcp_server # Terminal 2 — Streamlit chat UI streamlit run client/src/client/app.py ``` ### 🧠 Local Tools-Capable LLM Backend (for MCP testing) To exercise real tool-calling end-to-end against the MCP server, you need a local LLM backend that: - Exposes an **OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API** (for example, `/v1/chat/completions`), and - Supports OpenAI-style **`tools` / `tool_calls`**. A simple fully local option is [`llama-cpp-python`](https://github.com/abetlen/llama-cpp-python), which can run a quantized model on your machine and expose an OpenAI-compatible server. 1. **Install a local LLM server** Install `llama-cpp-python` in your environment (see its README for platform-specific build notes): ```bash pip install llama-cpp-python ``` 2. **Download a small tools-capable model** Download a small GGUF model that supports function/tool calling (for example, a 7B function-calling variant from Hugging Face) and note its path, e.g. `C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf`. 3. **Start the OpenAI-compatible server** Start the server and give the model a friendly alias that matches the default used by the Streamlit client (`client/src/client/app.py`): ```bash python -m llama_cpp.server \ --model "C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf" \ --model_alias local-tools-model \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 \ --chat_format openai ``` This exposes an OpenAI-style API at `http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1`. 4. **Configure the Streamlit client** `client/src/client/app.py` reads the following environment variables (with sensible defaults): | Variable | Default | |---|---| | `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8001/v1` | | `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | `local-tools-model` | | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | | `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | `local` | You can either set these in your shell or adjust them in the Streamlit sidebar under **"LLM Configuration"**. 5. **Verify tool-calling against the MCP server** - (Optional) Before starting the UI, confirm the LLM backend is reachable: ```bash curl http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1/models ``` If this request fails, fix your local LLM server configuration before debugging the MCP client/server. - Start the MCP server and Streamlit UI (either via `python -m client.run` or the split-terminal commands above). - In the browser UI, ask the assistant something that should use ODI tools, for example: *"Help me define a new Job-to-be-Done and add it to your ODI repository."* - You should see the assistant briefly display that it is calling tools (for example, `add_job`, `get_jobs`, etc.) and then respond with grounded ODI guidance, confirming that the local LLM, MCP server, and client wiring all work together. - If the LLM backend is unreachable or misconfigured, the UI will show a clear error banner indicating that the backend at your configured **Base URL** could not be reached, along with details from the underlying error. Use that message together with the steps above to fix your local LLM setup. ### 🤖 Agent-Driven Testing Type `/dev` in the AI assistant to trigger the full automated workflow: it will start both processes, open the browser, send a test message, and report the results. --- ## 🧹 Linting, Formatting & Type Checks (CI parity) The CI pipeline runs several quality checks. You can mirror them locally with: ```bash # Ruff lint and formatting checks (per-file config comes from each project's pyproject.toml) uv run ruff check . uv run ruff format --check . # Type checking (run per project so each project's config applies) uv run --directory core mypy . uv run --directory mcp_server mypy . uv run --directory local_server mypy . uv run --directory client mypy . uv run --directory cli mypy . uv run --directory connectors mypy . # Security scanning uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r core/src mcp_server/src local_server/src cli/src client/src connectors/src # Tests (same as CI) uv run --directory core pytest uv run --directory mcp_server pytest uv run --directory local_server pytest uv run --directory client pytest uv run --directory cli pytest uv run --directory connectors pytest ``` To run these automatically before each commit, enable the bundled pre-commit hooks: ```bash uv tool install pre-commit pre-commit install ``` After this, `ruff` and `ruff-format` will run on staged files whenever you commit. You can also trigger them manually with: ```bash pre-commit run --all-files ``` --- ## ✅ Testing Tests use **pytest** with **pytest-asyncio** (strict mode) and run entirely in-memory — no running server required. Each project owns its tests. CI runs the suite on Python **3.10, 3.11, and 3.12** and stores a coverage report as a build artifact: ```bash uv run --directory core pytest uv run --directory mcp_server pytest uv run --directory local_server pytest uv run --directory client pytest uv run --directory cli pytest uv run --directory connectors pytest ``` ### 📊 Test Coverage Map | File | What it covers | |---|---| | `core/tests/test_models.py` | Domain models and ODI opportunity-score computation | | `core/tests/test_service.py` | `ODIService` jobs/steps/outcomes and Customer Outcome CRUD | | `mcp_server/tests/test_odi.py` | Full ODI workflow (add job → steps → outcomes → retrieval) + capabilities tool | | `mcp_server/tests/test_customer_outcomes.py` | Customer Outcomes CRUD, filtering, computed opportunity scores, and tool validation | | `mcp_server/tests/test_server_tools.py` | Error handling and retrieval for the MCP tools | | `mcp_server/tests/test_tools.py` | Tool response-shape contract for `add_job` | | `local_server/tests/test_api.py` | Local FastAPI health endpoint | | `client/tests/test_run.py` | Dev launcher helpers (port checks) | | `cli/tests/test_cli.py` | CLI `--version` and `--help` behavior | | `cli/tests/test_outcomes_cli.py` | Customer Outcomes CLI subcommands with MCP stub | | `cli/tests/test_connectors_cli.py` | CLI `connectors` add/list/health/ingest adapter | | `connectors/tests/test_registry.py` | JSON connector registry persist/load and kind checks | | `connectors/tests/test_mcp_connector.py` | In-memory FastMCP health and ingest records | **Conventions:** - Test files live under each project's `tests/` directory and are named `test_*.py`. - Every async test is decorated with `@pytest.mark.asyncio`. - Use `Client(mcp)` directly (no HTTP server needed) for fast, isolated tests. - The server's `reset_db` autouse fixture clears in-memory state before each test. > [!TIP] > Type `/test` in the AI assistant to have the agent run all tests and report the results automatically. ### 🧪 Agent Session Tracking Agent sessions are captured with the [Entire](https://docs.entire.io/overview) CLI. The repository integration lives in `.entire/settings.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, and `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`. Run `entire status` to confirm it is enabled and `entire checkpoint list` to inspect captured checkpoints. --- ## 🤝 Superpowers with Pi This project includes [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) as a [Pi package](https://pi.dev/docs/packages). When using [Pi](https://pi.dev) with this project, Superpowers skills and extensions are automatically loaded. To enable: 1. Install Pi: `curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh` 2. Trust the project (first time only): `pi config --local --approve` 3. Start Pi: `pi` The `.pi/settings.json` declares the Superpowers package. Pi will clone it and load: - **Extension**: `superpowers.ts` — injects the `using-superpowers` bootstrap at session startup and after compaction - **Skills**: 12 Superpowers skills (TDD, subagent-driven-development, systematic-debugging, etc.) > [!NOTE] > Superpowers is also available for OpenCode via the plugin in `opencode.json`. The Pi package provides native Pi integration without needing the OpenCode compatibility layer. ### 🧼 Developer Workflow for Formatting - **When editing Python files**, either: - Rely on the **pre-commit hooks** above (recommended), or - Run Ruff formatting directly before pushing: ```bash uv run ruff format . ``` - **CI behavior**: - CI runs `uv run ruff check .` to lint without modifying files. - CI runs `uv run ruff format --check .` to *verify* formatting only. - If CI fails on formatting, run `uv run ruff format .` locally, commit the changes, and push again. +## 🤖 Superpowers with Freebuff + +This project ships [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) for [Freebuff](https://freebuff.com) as repo-local skills plus a session-start bootstrap. No plugin or hook is required: + +- **Skills**: `.agents/skills/` contains 15 Superpowers skills. +# Superpowers for Freebuff
+
+Freebuff uses the same [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) methodology as the OpenCode and Pi integrations, delivered through the two surfaces Freebuff loads automatically:
+
+1. **Skills** — `.agents/skills/` contains the 15 Superpowers skills. Freebuff scans `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md`, validates each frontmatter block, and lists every skill's name and description in the system prompt. The `skill` tool loads one by name.
+2. **Bootstrap** — `AGENTS.md` at the repository root carries the `using-superpowers` bootstrap, the Freebuff tool mapping, and a pointer to the project guardrails. Freebuff loads project `AGENTS.md` at session start, so the methodology is active without a plugin or hook. The section is explicitly scoped to Freebuff so OpenCode and Pi keep using their own integrations.
+3. **Reference mapping** — `.agents/skills/using-superpowers/references/freebuff-tools.md` is the detailed action-to-tool translation. `AGENTS.md` inlines the same mapping so it is present even before a skill is loaded.
+
+## Layout
+
+```text
+AGENTS.md                                        # session-start bootstrap + Freebuff mapping
+.agents/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md                  # 15 vendored Superpowers skills
+.agents/skills/using-superpowers/references/
+  freebuff-tools.md                              # detailed Freebuff tool mapping
+skills-lock.json                                 # source + hash for `npx skills update`
+```
+
+## First run
+
+Freebuff may ask whether to trust a repository's `.agents` directory the first time it sees one. Approve it interactively, or pass `--trust-agents` (intended for CI) when starting Freebuff.
+
+## Verify
+
+Start a fresh Freebuff session in this repository and ask:
+
+```text
+What are your superpowers?
+```
+
+The agent should know it has Superpowers and list the installed skills. The real acceptance check is:
+
+```text
+Let's make a react todo list
+```
+
+`brainstorming` must trigger before any code is written.
+
+## Updating
+
+The skill tree is committed, so a fresh clone needs no install step. To pull the latest Superpowers skills:
+
+```bash
+npx skills update -y
+```
+
+To reinstall from upstream:
+
+```bash
+npx skills add obra/superpowers --agent universal --skill '*' --copy -y
+```
+
+The `universal` target installs to `.agents/skills/`, which is the directory Freebuff scans. After an update, confirm `.agents/skills/using-superpowers/references/freebuff-tools.md` still exists; the `AGENTS.md` bootstrap is independent of the skill tree and survives skill updates.
+
+## Freebuff limitations
+
+- **No subagent tool.** Use `executing-plans` instead of `subagent-driven-development`, and run independent tasks sequentially instead of `dispatching-parallel-agents`.
+- **No plan mode.** Designs and plans are written to `docs/superpowers/specs/` and `docs/superpowers/plans/` with `write_file`.
+- **No session hooks.** `AGENTS.md` is the session-start surface; there is no plugin to install and no per-session opt-in.
+- **Compaction.** `write_todos` is a live view. Keep the durable ledger from `executing-plans` under `.superpowers/sdd/<plan-basename>/progress.md`.
